A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SonicMoE by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original H100 memory and throughput benchmarks, distributed training measurements, downstream language-model evaluations, and kernel and routing ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds B300 throughput benchmarks and component analyses in Section 6 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The documented algorithms receive limited corrections: Algorithm 4 returns rounded token lists and scores and removes its final unrounded gather, while Algorithm 3 corrects the weight-gradient product. The eight-kernel design, routing rule, and previously described Blackwell scheduling remain; these edits do not establish a new architecture or an implementation overhaul.

E1.justification: The systems evaluation expands from H100 to the distinct Blackwell B300 hardware environment across layer and component benchmarks. This substantially extends tested platform coverage. FineWeb-Edu, the eleven downstream tasks, and the evaluated model families remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds Triton's MoE/GEMM example to B300 comparisons, distinct from the Triton top-K comparator already evaluated in v1. Aggregation comparisons also add Gluon TMA gather and replace the single Triton summation control with max(tl.load, TMA). Existing routing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added B300 benchmarks use platform-specific microbatches: Table 9b specifies T=131072 and 81920 for the 1.4B and 7B configurations, versus 40960 and 24576 on H100. The revised H100 runtime breakdown also omits the formerly displayed DeepGEMM gradient-conversion stage. Language-model training budgets, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F substantially extends component analysis to Blackwell, testing fused versus unfused gathers along both GEMM dimensions and alternative aggregation-load implementations. These analyses examine whether the IO optimizations remain effective on the new architecture. Routing-sensitivity Tables 5–8 are retained, while v1's separate IO-cost-versus-granularity plot is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental results. Averages across tasks or configurations do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive B300 results, including reported 25% forward and 15% backward TFLOPS advantages over DeepGEMM++ for OLMoE-sized 7B models in Section 6.2.1 and Figure 12b. H100 DeepGEMM++ and DeepGEMM-pt backward totals change from 3.303/3.974 ms to 3.009/3.680 ms, alongside removal of the conversion segment. The downstream accuracy and routing-ablation table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 3 corrects dW2,e from A'e-transpose times dOe-transpose to A'e-transpose times dOe, consistent with the existing Appendix C derivation. Appendix C also corrects the per-token gradient dimension from T-by-d to 1-by-d. The arithmetic-intensity derivation and rounding bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary add a concrete Blackwell performance claim. The introduction revises the end-to-end training-throughput improvement from 50% to 42%, and the abstract explicitly limits the token-rounding speedup evidence to Hopper. The three central contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 extends the granularity-based performance interpretation to B300 and qualifies comparisons with Triton's inference-oriented implementation. It also removes substantive caveats, including v1's required score-separation assumption for FP32 top-K bit packing and discussion of hardware-dependent rounding tile sizes.

D1.justification: V2 documents Blackwell tile shapes and CLC scheduling, B300 configurations, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.6.0, and additional implementation-source pointers. Conversely, v1's index-prefetching diagram and accompanying register/shared-memory instructions disappear. These are documentation changes; the principal code and data access information is retained.

R1.justification: The Luo et al. Hopper microbenchmarking reference is removed. Appendix B expands the technical positioning against DeepGEMM to SM100 tiling and scheduling, and new Triton/Gluon implementation sources accompany the added comparisons. The broader MoE and routing research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 shortens method explanations, edits grammar and cross-references, moves the top-K section into Appendix D, and consolidates supporting material in Appendix E. The main section sequence and most of the narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Numerous performance figures become paired H100/B300 displays, Figure 1 gains a third panel, and new Blackwell scheduling and TMEM diagrams are added. The scaling-trends table and existing explanatory figures move to the appendix, while the IO-cost and index-prefetching figures are removed. This substantially changes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V1 describes Blackwell support without corresponding performance validation; v2 supplies substantial B300 benchmarks and component ablations against optimized DeepGEMM and Triton implementations. This closes an important gap in the claimed cross-platform efficiency. Corrected algorithm statements and the 50%-to-42% throughput claim improve consistency. These gains outweigh the limited loss of prefetching detail and the explicit top-K precision caveat.
